clue.text: Instant tea and coffee

parts.note: an instant is a moment, informally a mo
cha is a slang word for tea

explanation.surface: Someone orders a quick cuppa: instant tea and coffee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Instant' looks like a description of the drinks, but it is a noun here: a mo, a moment.
explanation.definitionFit: Mocha is a variety of coffee, named after the Yemeni port that once shipped it.

clue.text: Signal giving encouragement to prospective trader

definitions.meaning: a fire or light used as a warning or guiding sign
read as three words, '...!' urges a would-be dealer to become a confidence trickster

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper waves to draw in a would-be dealer.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half splits the answer into BE A CON, a cheer telling someone to turn con man, the 'trader' being a confidence trickster.
explanation.definitionFit: A beacon is a fire or light set up as a warning or guiding sign.

clue.text: The doorman identifies himself as an international swindler

definitions.text: The doorman identifies himself as an international swindler

parts.words: The doorman identifies himself as an international swindler
parts.note: a hotel porter introducing himself says '...', which run together names someone who brings goods in from abroad, a sound echoing impostor, a swindler

explanation.walkthrough: Spoken as one word, the doorman's self-introduction 'I'm porter' names a trader bringing goods from abroad, and also echoes 'impostor', the swindler.
explanation.definitionFit: An importer brings in goods from other countries, so trades internationally.

clue.text: Study an excursion in outline

parts.note: to con is an old word for to study or learn by heart
a tour is a trip or outing

explanation.surface: A student reads up on a day trip, sketching it in outline.
explanation.definitionFit: A contour is the outline or shape of something, as traced by a line on a map.

clue.text: Put the squeeze on Communist newspapers

parts.note: Com is a short form of Communist
the press means newspapers collectively

explanation.surface: The Communist party leans hard on the newspapers.
explanation.definitionFit: To compress is to squeeze or press something together.

clue.text: Harbour grudge against commercial traveller, and express it

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative who travels for a firm
to harbour a grudge against someone is to resent them

explanation.surface: A salesman nurses a grievance and lets it out.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue gives the grudge before the traveller, but the answer puts REP first; 'and' and 'it' only link.
explanation.definitionFit: To represent something is to depict or set it forth, to express it.

clue.text: Darling little Maureen on holiday with her new husband

parts.note: honey is a term of endearment, like darling
Mo is a short form of the name Maureen

explanation.surface: Sweet little Maureen is off on her wedding trip.
explanation.definitionFit: A honeymoon is the trip a newly married couple take together.

clue.text: Was too fond of telling Mr Heath to take action

parts.note: do means act or take action
Ted Heath was the British Conservative Prime Minister of 1970 to 1974

explanation.surface: Someone, besotted, urges the Prime Minister to get on with it.
explanation.walkthrough: The telling is the command 'Do, Ted!', addressed to Edward (Ted) Heath, a British Prime Minister.
explanation.definitionFit: To dote on someone is to love them to excess, uncritically.

clue.text: Graduate over fifty-one in an African country

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits over the second

parts.note: an MA is a Master of Arts, a graduate
LI is 51 in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A graduate tops fifty-one somewhere in Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Mali is a landlocked nation in West Africa.

clue.text: Examine a supermarket counter

definitions.meaning: to check something out is to look into it
the till point where shoppers pay

explanation.definitionFit: To check out means to inspect; the checkout is the till where shoppers pay on leaving.

clue.text: To aim high is a feature of the church

parts.note: a spire is the tapering tower on a church roof

explanation.surface: Ambition is likened to the church's tall steeple.
explanation.definitionFit: To aspire is to have lofty ambitions, to strive upward.

clue.text: Fly from a Chinese dynasty in retreat

indicators.note: retreating means going backwards, so the dynasty's name is read from its end

parts.note: the Tang dynasty ruled China from 618 to 907

explanation.surface: Someone flees from a retreating Chinese dynasty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fly' looks like a verb, but it is the insect; 'in retreat' turns TANG round.
explanation.definitionFit: A gnat is a small two-winged insect, a kind of fly.

clue.text: All the things I found in a French poem

indicators.note: the letter I is located inside the French word plus poem

parts.note: un is French for a
verse is poetry, a poem

explanation.surface: Everything I need turns up in a French poem.
explanation.definitionFit: The universe is everything that exists, the whole of creation.

clue.text: Rash declaration that Tess's creator is an idiot

parts.note: a fool is an idiot
Thomas Hardy wrote Tess of the d'Urbervilles

explanation.surface: A hasty critic calls the author of Tess a fool.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'declaration' is the statement 'Fool, Hardy': the pieces come out in reverse of the clue's order.
explanation.definitionFit: Foolhardy means recklessly bold, careless of danger.

clue.text: Small change from officers of the law

explanation.surface: Loose coins taken off the police.
explanation.definitionFit: Coppers are both low-value coins and, informally, policemen.

clue.text: Its fragrance might cause one to think about mother

indicators.note: the word for think goes around the word for mother

parts.note: to ponder is to think
ma is mother

explanation.surface: A scent makes someone think of their mother.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a loose description rather than a synonym: the clue says what a scented ball might make you do, and 'about' reads as 'concerning' but signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: A pomander is a perfumed ball carried or hung to give a sweet smell.

clue.text: Here is the donation

explanation.definitionFit: Present means in attendance, and as a noun a gift.

clue.text: Remembered being summoned for an encore

definitions.meaning: called back on stage by the audience

explanation.surface: A performer remembers being called back for more.
explanation.definitionFit: Recalled means brought to mind, and also called back, as a performer for an encore.

clue.text: Rust found in the central shaft

indicators.note: the shaft goes inside the word for central part

parts.note: the core is the central part
a rod is a shaft or bar

explanation.surface: Corrosion is discovered in a machine's central shaft.
explanation.definitionFit: To rust is to corrode, eaten away by oxidation.

clue.text: Passionate love for a bird

parts.note: flaming can mean ardent or fiery
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone has an ardent affection for a feathered friend.
explanation.definitionFit: A flamingo is a tall pink wading bird.

clue.text: Standard rejection by the marines

parts.note: no is a refusal
RM stands for the Royal Marines

explanation.surface: The marines turn down the usual practice.
explanation.definitionFit: A norm is a standard or usual pattern.

clue.text: Manage to lay top course of wall

definitions.meaning: a builder's term: to put the coping, the top layer, on a wall

explanation.surface: Someone manages to finish off the top of a wall.
explanation.definitionFit: To cope is to manage; in building it means to cap a wall with its top layer of stones.

clue.text: Scheme by retired artist is on the level

parts.note: a plan is a scheme

indicators.note: retiring means withdrawing backwards, so the artist's letters are turned round

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A painter's retirement plan is honest and above board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the level' suggests honest, but it means flat.
explanation.definitionFit: Planar means lying in a single flat plane, level.

clue.text: Benjamin appears before church magistrates

indicators.note: one piece is placed ahead of the other in the answer

parts.note: Ben is a short form of Benjamin

explanation.surface: Benjamin comes before a church court.
explanation.definitionFit: The bench is the collective term for judges or magistrates in court.

clue.text: Gentleman accommodates old queen in style

indicators.note: to accommodate is to take in, so the title holds the queen inside

parts.note: Mr is the title of a gentleman
Anne was Queen of Great Britain from 1702 to 1714

explanation.surface: A gentleman stylishly plays host to an aged queen.
explanation.definitionFit: Manner is a way or style of doing something.

clue.text: Let out and let out again

explanation.surface: Something is freed and then freed again.
explanation.definitionFit: Released means set free; split as re-leased it means rented out once more.

clue.text: Publicity agents have the last word about departmental head

indicators.note: the last word goes around the department's head letter

parts.note: amen is said at the end of a prayer

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Advertisers get the final say over the department chief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'departmental head' looks like a boss, but it is just the letter D.
explanation.definitionFit: Admen are people who work in advertising.

clue.text: Wanting to be free of work is just a day-dream

definitions.text: Wanting to be free of work
definitions.meaning: a fancy, or wish, to be idle

explanation.surface: Wishing for no work is just a pipe dream.
explanation.definitionFit: An idle fancy is a pointless whim; read literally it is a liking for idleness.
